title: Cold Start - brackenlanegarage.net
description: The website of Cold Start, a four-piece bar band out of Gridfall, built and maintained by the bass player: three upcoming dates, a page of songs nobody can listen to, one shirt, and a news page that stopped last October.

blocks.text: *** NEXT SHOW: TILBY'S, DEPOT STREET, GRIDFALL, FRIDAY 2 OCTOBER, 9PM, NO COVER *** KERRIN FIRE HALL 24 OCTOBER, DINNER FIRST ***

blocks.caption: Curt's garage on Bracken Lane with the door up. That is how we practice from April to about the middle of October, and it is why this website is called what it is.

blocks.body:
We are a four piece out of Gridfall. We play bars, fire company dinners, the Grange, one street fair a year and anything else with two outlets on separate circuits and a floor that will take a drum kit.

The band is called [b]Cold Start[/b]. It was called Bracken Lane until 2021, and by then I had already paid for this domain name, and I am not paying for a second one. Curt's garage is on Bracken Lane. That is the whole story and people ask about it every single show.

Most of what we play is other people's. Some of it is ours. You cannot hear ours anywhere, and there is [url=/music]a whole page about why[/url].

items: Four of us. Two guitars, bass, drums. No horns, no fiddle, no keyboard since 2018. We have been asked about all three.
Three hours with two breaks, or two hours straight through. Whichever suits the room.
We bring the PA and we run it ourselves. Nobody has to find you a sound man.
We are loud, but we are not stupid about it. If you come up and ask us to come down, we come down, and we do not make a face about it.
$350 for a bar, less for the fire companies, and the [url=/booking]booking page[/url] has the rest of it in plain numbers.

head: When
Where
What it is
rows: 9pm to midnight, three sets. No cover. 21 and over. The kitchen shuts at ten, so eat first.
Kerrin Ambulance Association roast beef dinner. They serve 5 to 7, we play 7 to 10. $12 at the door and that includes the dinner, which is the best twelve dollars on this page.
8 to 11. $5 at the door. Covered dish if you feel like it. The Grange does the coffee and will not let you pay for it.

blocks.body:
That is everything that is booked. [url=/shows]The shows page[/url] has the details and a list of everywhere we have played since we started keeping one.

If you drove somewhere to see us and we were not there, I am sorry, and it has happened twice, and both times it was a listing somebody's computer wrote and not us. There is a paragraph about that on the shows page too.

Curt Mowery on drums, Randy Pelkey on guitar, Mike Cottrill on guitar and most of the singing, and me on bass. [url=/band]There is a page[/url] with who does what for a living, which in one case matters, because Mike is on call for the water district and has gone out in the middle of a show and not come back twice.

We have been the same four since the autumn of 2018. Before that there were five of us.

Email: [b]coldstart@verity.net[/b]

That comes to me. I read it Sunday nights at the kitchen table, so if you write on a Monday you are waiting six days for an answer and I am sorry about that. If it is about a date that is more than three weeks out, email is fine and I will answer it that Sunday.

If it is about [i]this[/i] week, do not email. Telephone Curt at the bus garage in Kerrin during the day, or telephone me at home after six, and both numbers are in the county book under our own names because neither of us has ever had an unlisted number in our lives.

We are not on any of the social sites. Curt's wife Denise puts the dates up on [url=synth://verityfeed.social/]VerityFeed[/url] when she remembers, and she remembers about half the time, which is better than I manage here.

The counter came with the template in 2019 and I have never touched it. A fair share of it is me, checking whether the page I just changed looks the way I meant it to, and another share of it is whatever crawls this site at four in the morning, because the host's log says something does, every night, for years, and it is not a person in Verity County.

[i]Last changed Wednesday 2 September 2026. The [url=/news]news page[/url] has had nothing real on it since last October, which is on me and not on the website.[/i]

-- Brian Ottmar, bass

blocks.caption: The four of us in the bay at the Kerrin Fire Hall, October 2024, before doors. Denise took it. Randy is squinting because Randy is always squinting.

blocks.body: Four people who have all lived in this county their entire lives, in a garage, on a Tuesday, since the first week of March 2016. Nobody here is trying to get anywhere. Two of us have kids in the Kerrin school and one of us fixes its buses.

46. Started on a kit his uncle left in a barn in Cobb and has not been without one since he was thirteen.

Mechanic at the bus garage for the Kerrin consolidated school, twenty-two years this January. If you have a child on a north-end bus, Curt has had that bus on a lift, and he will tell you it is a good bus, because he would not sign it off otherwise.

The garage on Bracken Lane is his. It is a two-car garage with one car in it, a bench down the whole back wall, a kerosene heater we do not run while we play because the fan is louder than Randy, and a Ludwig kit from 1974 that came out of a church hall in Halsey with a snare from 2009 on it. He has one cymbal he will not let anybody else pack.

He does not sing. We have tried for ten years and we are going to stop trying.

44. That is me, and I built this website, so anything on it that is wrong is mine and you should tell me about it.

I drive for [url=synth://dorrancepropane.synth/]Dorrance Propane[/url], five days and every third Saturday, which is the one thing that has ever cost us a booking. Twelve years on the truck. Before that I was at the co-op yard.

I play a Precision copy I bought used in Marchfield in 1999 for $180 and have never wanted to replace, through a cabinet Randy found for us [url=synth://gridfall-buysell.net/]on Buy & Sell[/url] for $110 with one blown speaker, which I replaced for $46. I also run the PA, carry the PA, do the merch, answer the email and keep this site, and that sounds like more than it is. It is mostly carrying.

I learned HTML in about 2003 off a library book and it turns out very little of it has changed, or at least the part I use has not.

49. Plays most of the lead, all of the solos, and the parts of the rhythm Mike cannot get to because he is singing.

Runs Pelkey Small Engine out of a shop behind his house on the Halsey road, and has had his hands inside half the mowers, blowers, tillers and pressure washers in the south end of this county. He is closed Sundays and Mondays and he is not going to look at your chainsaw at a gig, although people do bring them up.

Amplifier is a 1978 combo he bought in 1994 for $200. It has been re-tubed twice, re-coned once, and had the reverb tank replaced with one out of a different amplifier entirely, which is why it sounds the way it does. He will not play through anything else and we have stopped suggesting it.

He is the loudest of us and he knows it and we have an agreed hand signal, and the hand signal works about seventy percent of the time.

45. Sings nearly all of it and wrote most of what is ours.

Weekdays, and every other weekend on call, he is the Verity County water district's certified operator for Kerrin and the Nye Mills line. Two wells off Kerrin Road, a 150,000 gallon tower, forty-some miles of main, about 900 connections. On a Tuesday there are three of them. On a Saturday night at nine o'clock there is Mike, and the next certified operator is forty minutes away in the next county under a mutual aid letter that has been used four times.

So he carries the district phone on stage. It sits on the amp. If it goes off in the middle of a song he finishes the song, and then he goes, and there is no argument about it and there never has been.

He would like everyone reading this to know two things. One, the county will test your private well for bacteria and nitrates for free, the kit is free, and hardly anybody does it: [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/well-water]here is the page[/url]. Two, if your water goes brown after a hydrant flush, run the cold tap in the basement for ten minutes, and do not run the washing machine, and it is not dangerous, it is iron.

blocks.text: Terry Vosburgh, who is not in the band any more

blocks.body:
Rhythm guitar and a Wurlitzer, 2016 to 2018. Moved 400 miles to be near his daughter and the two grandchildren and has not been back except at Thanksgiving.

He wrote [url=/music]Second Shift[/url], which is still the best thing any of us have got and is not even close, and we still play it, and he knows we still play it because Curt telephones him about once a season and tells him.

We did not replace him. Four is easier to fit in a garage, and easier to divide $350 by.

Seven until half past nine, in the garage, every week that Mike is not on call and Curt is not covering a late run and I am not on the Saturday rota, which works out to about thirty-five Tuesdays a year.

We run through whatever is coming up, we argue about tempo, Randy plays something nobody asked for, and at about ten past nine Curt's neighbor Frank comes out and stands in his own driveway with a beer, which is his way of saying it is nine o'clock, and he has never once complained to anybody about anything. We put the door down at half past.
Three on the book. If you want us for something, the [url=/booking]booking page[/url] is the fastest way to find out whether we can do it and what it costs.

blocks.text: Friday 2 October 2026 -- Tilby's, Depot Street, Gridfall

blocks.body:
9pm to midnight. Three sets, two breaks. No cover. 21 and over after 8 and they mean it now, they got a talking-to in the spring.

The kitchen closes at ten. If you want the fish you want to be there by half past nine, and if you are coming for the fish and not for us we do not mind and neither does Dean.

Parking is the lot behind, and the two spaces at the end by the fence are the ones they tow, not the rest. That sign has been wrong since it went up.

The Kerrin Ambulance Association's roast beef dinner. Dinner 5 to 7, we play 7 to 10. $12 at the door and that is the dinner as well.

This is the fifth year we have done this one and it is the one we would keep if we had to keep only one. It is a fire hall floor, it is families until about half eight and then it is not, and the money goes to an ambulance service staffed by people who have got out of bed at three in the morning for somebody on this page.

We play it for $150 and the Association has tried twice to pay us more, and Curt has said no twice.

Bring cash for the raffle. They do not take cards and the machine they were promised in 2023 never came.

blocks.text: Saturday 12 December 2026 -- Ashkettle Grange Hall, Route 62

blocks.body:
8 to 11. $5 at the door, under 12 free, covered dish if you want to bring one and nobody counts.

The Grange hall is out Route 62 past the Ashkettle turn, on the left, and the sign is small and unlit and you will go past it, everybody does. If you get to the quarry cut you have gone about two miles too far.

One warning for December: the hall has electric baseboard and one stove and it takes until about half past nine to warm up. Keep your coat for the first set. We do.

Randy's amp buzzes in that hall and has every time since 2019. Between songs in the second set you can hear numbers out of it, the four-digit ones, same as anybody parked out there with a radio on gets. It has nothing to do with us and I have replaced the cable twice. It is just what that hall does.
I started keeping this list when somebody at the Legion asked how long we had been at it and none of us could answer. Before 2022 there were maybe fifteen more and I have not got the dates.

Coyne Flats Days, Main Street stage
First bar show in two and a half years. Rusty, loud, fine.

blocks.text: Two nights people drove somewhere and we were not there

blocks.body:
In March last year a weekend listings piece on one of the county sites had us at the Wheelhouse in Halsey. The Wheelhouse shut in January 2024. Three people I know of drove out there, and one of them was from Milbrook, which is forty minutes.

I wrote to the site. What came back was a paragraph thanking me for my interest in local coverage and telling me that listings are assembled automatically from publicly available sources, and that corrections may be submitted through the appropriate channel, and it did not say what the channel was. The listing came back the next week with the same venue and the date moved. It is off now. I do not know whether that is because of anything I did.

The second one was last autumn and it was our fault as much as anything: we cancelled a Tilby's date and I did not take it off this page for nine days.

So: [b]this page is the only listing we keep[/b]. If something somewhere else says we are playing and it is not on here, it is wrong, and you can telephone Curt and he will tell you so. A lot of what is written about this county now is written by something that has never been in it, and most of the time that only costs somebody a trip to Halsey.

blocks.text: Places we used to play that are not there

items: The Wheelhouse, Halsey. Shut January 2024. Best room we ever played, a long low bar with a proper stage and a ceiling that did something right, and it is a storage unit business now.
Coyne Flats VFW pavilion. The post gave the pavilion up in 2025 and the county mows it.
The Marchfield Moose. Still open, does not have bands any more, and that is a rule and not a snub.
The Gridfall Elks, which never had us, and I am told still has a piano nobody plays.

blocks.body:
[b]There is nothing on this page you can listen to.[/b]

I want to say that at the top, because people click through expecting a player and there is not one, and there has not been one since 2021, and I would rather you knew before you scrolled.

What there is instead is a list of the eight songs that are ours, what they are, how long they run and who wrote them. If you have heard us you have heard most of these. If you have not, this is the closest thing that exists.

head: Song
Runs
Written by
Recorded?
rows: Three goes at it. None of them exist.
Mike, and I did the second verse
All of us, in the garage, over about a month
A phone recording that is gone.
Once, 2019, and that is the one I am sorriest about.

blocks.body:
Three minutes forty-one. The one the band is named after, or the other way round, depending on which of us you ask and Randy will tell you it was the song first.

It is about a truck that will not turn over in a yard at five in the morning in February, and the man standing next to it deciding whether that is a problem with the truck or a problem with the whole arrangement. It does not answer that. It just goes to the chorus.

It opens with Randy on his own for eight bars, then Curt comes in with the kick on its own for four, and then the rest of it. Live it is the third or fourth song, because it takes a room that has already warmed up. In the garage it is the first thing we play every single Tuesday and has been for six years.

Four minutes six. Mike wrote it standing in a hole on Kerrin Road on the 24th of December, and it is the only song we have that I would call funny, although he does not play it as though it is funny, which is why it works.

A six inch cast iron main from 1961 let go under the road at about eleven at night on Christmas Eve. He was out there until half four in the morning with a contractor's hoe and two men from the highway garage, in the rain, and about sixty houses had no water, and at some point somebody came out in a dressing gown to ask how long it would be, and he told them the truth, which was that he did not know.

The chorus is him telling them he does not know. That is all it is. Four verses and the same answer each time.

It is the only one of ours that people request.

Four minutes fifty-two, which is too long, and we know it is too long, and we are not cutting it.

The last freight over the branch went on the fourteenth of March 2008, Marchfield down to Coyne Flats. Mike's father worked on that line for nineteen years, not at the end, in the middle. The song is the son standing at the Quarry Road crossing on the last morning with about eleven other people, which is genuinely how many were there, and nobody knowing what to do with their hands.

The gates came down that autumn. There is a bike trail on it now and it is a good trail, and the song does not say one word against the trail, which took some doing, because Randy wanted it to.

Mike wrote all of it except the second verse, which I wrote, and mine is the weakest part of the song and everybody in the band is too polite to say so twice.

Two fifty-eight. Fast, two chords for most of it, and the only thing we have that you could dance to without trying.

It is about driving the length of Kerrin Road at night and nothing happening. That is not a description of the song, that is the song. Randy wrote it in about twenty minutes and it is better than things Mike has worked on for a year, and this is a source of some feeling in the garage.

We open with it. Always have.

Six twenty on a good night, and in June 2024 it was seventeen minutes, because Mike's phone went off in the second verse and left Randy and Curt and me to fill until he got back, and he did not get back.

Slow one. The four of us built it out of a thing Curt was doing at the end of a practice, and it is the only one where every one of us wrote some of it, which is also why it took a month.

There is a long instrumental in the middle that changes every time and has never once been played the same way, and that is the part people talk about after, and none of us can tell you what is in it.

Three twelve. Terry wrote it in 2017 and left in 2018 and it is still the best song this band has.

It is a man coming off a second shift at a place that is closing in six weeks, and it is not angry, and it does not have a speech in it, and that is exactly what is good about it. The last line is him deciding not to say anything to anybody in the car park, and going home.

We play it every show. Terry knows. Curt rings him.

This is the one we did record properly, in 2019, on a borrowed eight-track in the Grange hall, and I will get to what happened to that in a minute and it is going to sound stupid.

About two and a half minutes. Instrumental, unfinished, and it has been unfinished since 2021.

Randy has a riff and a middle and no end, and every few months he plays it at the end of a practice and we all have a go at an ending, and none of them are right. We have never played it in front of anybody. We probably never will.

It is named for the cut out past Ashkettle, where the old quarry road goes through, because that is where he was when he thought of it, which was sitting in a truck waiting for a man who never turned up. There is a [url=synth://quarrycut.net/]page somebody keeps about the cut[/url] that is worth ten minutes if you have never been out there.

Three twenty, or four forty, depending on whether Mike sings the first verse twice, which is what he does, because there is no second verse and there has never been a second verse.

He has had the first verse since 2022. It is good. The second one has not come and he will not write a bad one to get it finished, and I respect that and it also drives Curt up the wall.

We have played it live about forty times and I would say four people have noticed.

blocks.text: So why can you not hear any of it

blocks.body:
Three goes at recording, three different ways of coming to nothing. None of them are anybody's fault except in the ordinary way where everything is somebody's fault.

[b]2019, the Grange hall.[/b] A fellow Terry knew brought an eight-track and two decent microphones and gave us a Saturday for nothing. We got four songs down: Second Shift, Cold Start, Kerrin Road and one of Terry's we do not play any more. It came to me as files and I put them on the laptop and put a copy on the free tier of a backup service, because that is what you did.

The laptop died in February 2021. Not dropped, not spilled on, it just would not come on again, and the fellow in Gridfall who looks at them said the drive was gone and I believe him.

The backup service had closed in the November before that. They emailed about it. I can see now that they emailed about it, because I went and looked, and it is there, in with the receipts, sent on a Tuesday in September 2020, and I did not open it. Ninety days to download your files, it says. I had four hundred and eleven days of not opening an email.

[b]2023, a studio.[/b] $180 for an evening in a room in the state capital, which is two hours each way on a Wednesday. We got Six Inch Main and Cold Start. The playing is fine. The vocal microphone was set wrong the whole night and nobody caught it, and what came back sounds like Mike singing through a door. The man was decent about it and offered us another evening at half price. We have not been back. It is not the $90. It is the four hours.

[b]2025, the Grange hall again.[/b] Curt's nephew brought a recorder that takes a card and we did four songs after the show on the 18th of October, at about half eleven at night, in an empty hall, and I have never heard us play better and neither has Randy.

The card had nothing readable on it. We have had two people look at it. One of them got the file lengths back, which are right, and nothing else.

That is the one that still bothers me.

blocks.text: What is left of the 2019 files

blocks.body: This is what was on this page from 2019 until the host change, and I have left it here because taking it off felt like agreeing to something. The player stopped working years ago. The filenames are right, they just are not anywhere.

blocks.text: There are forty seconds of us on the internet

blocks.body:
Somebody at Tilby's in June held a phone up during Nobody's On The Lake and it ended up on [url=synth://clipvault-shorts.tv/]the short video site[/url], vertical, forty-one seconds, mostly the back of a man's head.

It says 4,100 views. There has never been a room with 4,100 people in it that had us in it, and there is not going to be. The caption calls us a different band, one word off, and the comments underneath are eleven identical sentences about how nobody makes music like this any more, posted by accounts with numbers on the end of their names, and one from somebody in the county saying [i]that's Tilby's[/i], which is the only true thing under it.

I am not going to ask them to take it down. It is forty seconds and it is the only forty seconds there is.

We have about forty. I am not listing forty. What you will get on a three-set night:

A fair amount out of 1969 to 1979, because that is what the rooms we play want and it is also what we grew up with in other people's cars. Four or five from the eighties that everybody sings. Two country ones that Mike does properly and does not send up. One instrumental in the second set while Mike gets a drink of water.

We do not do the long one with the eagle in it. Not out of principle. We have never learned it and every time somebody shouts for it we agree in the van that we should learn it, and then it is Tuesday and we do not.

items: First set is covers, start to finish, from about 9 to 9:50. People are still arriving and eating and nobody wants to hear a new song from four men they can see in the daylight at the hardware store.
Second set has Kerrin Road at the top, two or three more of ours through the middle, and Six Inch Main before the last cover, because by then somebody has shouted for it.
Third set is whatever the room is. If they are dancing we do not stop. If they are sitting we do Nobody's On The Lake and Fourteenth of March and let it be quiet.
Last song is Second Shift, always, and we do not do encores, because the lights come up at midnight and Dean wants to be home.

blocks.body: There is one shirt. There has been one shirt since 2023 and there is not going to be a second one until this one is gone.

blocks.caption: The shirt. Ash grey, black print, the Kerrin water tower on the front and nothing on the back.

blocks.body:
Ash grey. Black ink, one colour, front only. The Kerrin tower with COLD START under it in the same letters that are on the tower, and nothing on the back, because a back print was another $2.10 a shirt and there were already going to be too many of them.

Mike's cousin Dawn drew the tower off a photograph and did not charge us, and she got the legs right, which matters later on this page.

They are a heavyweight shirt, they came out of the box a bit big in the body, and three years of people wearing them says they do not shrink much. Printed by a shop in Halsey that does the school's track shirts.

[b]$15.[/b] $18 for 2XL and 3XL, because that is what the printer charges us and we are not clever enough to hide it in the price of the others.

head: Size
Left
Note
rows: We ordered thirty-six smalls out of a run of seventy-two. Thirty-six. I did the order form.
Left over from a run Denise had done for her nephew's team and paid for herself.

blocks.body:
The count is from the second week of August and it is a box in Curt's garage, so it is right to within one or two.

If you want a large or an extra large: we will do another run when the smalls are under ten, and at twenty-three that is not this year, and I am not sorry enough about it to eat the cost of sixty shirts.

items: At a show. Cash. The box is on the end of the merchandise table which is also where the PA case is, and whoever is not playing is watching it, which is nobody, so shout.
From Curt at the bus garage in Kerrin, weekdays, if you do not mind walking into a bus garage.

By post. Send a cheque made out to [b]B. Ottmar[/b] for $15 plus $4 postage, with your size and your address on a piece of paper, to Cold Start, PO Box 118, Gridfall. I post them on Saturday mornings. It has worked eleven times and gone wrong once, and that once was the post office and not me.
We do not take cards. We had a payment button on this page for fourteen months in 2023 and 2024. It cost $9 a month. We sold three shirts through it.

blocks.body:
In 2023 the printer had a deal where 100 koozies were $74 if you were already ordering shirts, and I said yes to that on a Tuesday night without asking anybody.

We have 71 koozies.

They are free. Take one. Take four. If you are having a party, telephone me and I will bring you twenty, and I am not joking and I would like the shelf back.

blocks.text: The shirt that is not our shirt

blocks.body:
Since about February there has been a site selling a shirt with our name on it for $32.99 plus shipping, in eleven colours and up to 5XL, printed when somebody orders it. It is [url=synth://bandmerchdirect.shop/]bandmerchdirect.shop[/url] and I am linking it only so you can see what I am talking about.

We get nothing from it. That is not the main thing though. The main thing is that the picture is wrong: whatever redrew it gave the tower four legs, and the Kerrin tower has three, and it has had three since 1968, and every single person on the north end of this county knows it has three.

I wrote to them in March. The reply thanked me for my message and said my enquiry had been received and would be handled in the order it was received. In August I wrote again. The reply was word for word the same reply, including a reference number, and it was the same reference number.

Buy the $15 one off Curt. It is a better shirt and the tower is right.

[i]I know. The last thing on here that is actually news is from October last year. Everything since then is housekeeping and I am not going to pretend otherwise by putting a date on the top of the page.[/i]
testing

blocks.text: Sunday 19 April 2026 -- new host, and a page about us that is wrong

blocks.body:
The old host put their price up to $58 a year and I have moved us to one that is $38, and everything came across except the guestbook dates, which are now all one day out, and I am not fixing 40 entries by hand.

While I was doing that I found a page about us on one of those sites that has a page about everybody. It is worth reading, because I cannot work out where a single sentence of it came from.

[quote=Songpage artist profile]Cold Start is a rock band from Gridfall, Verity County. The group was formed in 2004 in the aftermath of the Gridfall power station fire, a tragedy which claimed two lives and which continues to shape the region's musical identity. Drawing on the working-class traditions of the American heartland, the band has become a fixture of the local live circuit. Fans of the group should also explore the wider Verity County music scene.[/quote]

We started in Curt's garage in March 2016.

The fire was the 11th of June 2003 and it was a substation, not a power station, and it was at Depot and Quarry Road and you can walk past it. Nobody died. Two of the Gridfall volunteers took in smoke and went to County General and were home the same afternoon. Every man on this page had people at work that day, and the year is not a thing that is in dispute here, and I do not know how you write a paragraph about a county without asking one person who lives in it.

The site is [url=synth://songpage-artists.biz/]songpage-artists.biz[/url]. There is a contact form. I filled it in twice.

blocks.text: Saturday 18 October 2025 -- we recorded four songs and we have nothing

blocks.body:
Grange hall, after the show, hall empty, about half eleven at night. Curt's nephew Trevor brought a recorder and two stands and we did Second Shift, Cold Start, Six Inch Main and Fourteenth of March, twice each, and the second take of Six Inch Main is the best I have heard us play in ten years.

The card has nothing readable on it. Trevor has had two goes at it and a fellow at the school has had a go at it. The file lengths come back and they are the right lengths. That is all there is.

I am not going to write a paragraph about how that feels. We are going to do it again in the spring.

The Ambulance Association did 190 roast beef dinners, which is the most they have ever done, and they ran out of horseradish at about ten past six and sent a man to Gridfall for more.

We played 7 to 10. Mike's phone did not go off. The raffle took $612 and the new cot mattress they were raising for is bought and in the rig.

blocks.text: Saturday 12 July 2025 -- Coyne Flats Days, and the 8 o'clock slot at last

blocks.body:
Four years of the 4pm family slot and this year they gave us 8pm, and it is a different thing at 8pm, and we did five of our own, which is the most we have ever done in front of people who did not come to see us.

Six Inch Main got a shout from somewhere near the chip van and Mike laughed in the middle of a line, which you would only notice if you knew.

blocks.text: Sunday 16 March 2025 -- somebody listed us at a place that has been shut for a year

blocks.body:
A things-to-do-this-weekend piece on one of the county news sites had us at the Wheelhouse in Halsey on the Saturday. The Wheelhouse shut in January 2024. We were at the Eagles in Marchfield.

Three people drove to Halsey. One came from Milbrook. He telephoned Curt about it and was very decent about it, which made it worse.

I wrote to the site through the only address on it and got a paragraph back about publicly available sources. The listing appeared again the week after with the date moved forward. It is gone now and I do not know why.

There are four or five sites doing weekend listings for this county now and as far as I can tell not one of them has a person on it. [url=synth://veritycountytoday.com/]One of them[/url] I have written to twice.

Snow started at four. Nine people at Tilby's, four of them us, and Dean said play or do not play, either way you are getting paid, because he is Dean.

We played two sets for five people and it was one of the better nights of the year. You can hear everything in a room that empty. We did Ninety Days and Mike sang the one verse twice and afterwards a woman at the bar asked what the second verse was and Mike told her the truth.

blocks.text: Sunday 17 November 2024 -- the Grange got the roof

blocks.body:
The Ashkettle Grange fundraiser in November brought in enough with the auction and the door that the roof is going on in the spring, and it went on in the spring, and the hall did not leak all last winter for the first time since anybody can remember.

We took $100 for that one instead of $250 and would have taken nothing.

Mike's phone went off in the second verse of Nobody's On The Lake at Tilby's on Saturday. A hydrant got hit on Kerrin Road and the district lost pressure on the north leg.

He unplugged, said into the microphone that he was sorry and that it was the water, and went, and he was gone the rest of the night, and the three of us played the middle of that song for eleven minutes and then finished the set without a singer.

People clapped. Somebody bought Randy a drink. Randy has mentioned it since.

blocks.text: Monday 15 January 2024 -- the Wheelhouse is shut

blocks.body:
We played the Wheelhouse in Halsey on Saturday night and nobody told us until we were loading out that it was the last Saturday. Jeanine told Curt at the door with the cash box in her hand.

Twenty-six years. It was the best room in this county to play in, a long low bar with a real stage and a ceiling that did something for the sound that no fire hall does, and we were in it six times and thought there would be a seventh.

That is the fourth room we have played that has gone. I am not going to list them here because there is a list of them on [url=/shows]the shows page[/url] and one list is enough.

Sold eleven at Kerrin on the Saturday, which at $15 is $165, and the run cost $402 for 72 shirts, so there is a while to go yet.

The box is in Curt's garage under the bench. Sizes and what is left are on [url=/merch]the merch page[/url] and I will keep that honest.

blocks.text: Sunday 22 May 2022 -- first bar show in two and a half years

blocks.body:
Tilby's on Saturday, the 21st, and it was the first time the four of us had been on a stage since the winter before all that. Rusty in the first set and fine by the third.

We have kept practising the whole way through, in the garage, with the door up, and the neighbours put up with it, and I want that written down somewhere.

blocks.text: Saturday 18 September 2021 -- we are called Cold Start now

blocks.body:
Five years of being Bracken Lane and there are two other bands called some version of it, one of them four counties away and playing the same kind of rooms, and a booker rang Curt in the spring wanting to know which one we were.

So: Cold Start, after Randy's song, decided in the garage in about twenty minutes with one vote against and Randy will not say who.

The website stays where it is. coldstart.net is parked by a firm that wants [url=synth://nameharbor.hostline/offer/coldstart-net]$2,400 for it[/url] and has wanted that since before we existed. This address costs me $18 a year and everybody in the county who needs it already has it written down.

Put this up over two evenings off a template. If anything on it looks wrong on your machine, tell me at a show and tell me what you are looking at it on, because I only have the one computer to check with.

Dates go on the shows page. Songs will go on the music page when we have got something to put there.

Email [b]coldstart@verity.net[/b] and I will answer on the Sunday. If the date is inside three weeks, telephone Curt at the Kerrin bus garage in the day, because I will not see the email in time.

We are four men with jobs. Nothing on this page is negotiable in a way that will surprise you and nothing on it is a trick.

head: Price
Notes
rows: Within about 25 miles of Gridfall. That is the four of us, the PA and somebody to run it.
Fire company, ambulance association, Grange or the Legion
Any of them, any distance in this county. If the night is for a piece of equipment, ask us and we will very likely do it for the gas.
Private party, barn, shed, back field
We have played all three. Bring us to look at the power first.
That is fuel and the fact that we are unloading at two in the morning on a work night.
And read the bit below before you ask.

blocks.body:
Cash or a cheque on the night, to B. Ottmar, and I split it four ways in the van before we pull out of the car park, which is a habit from a band Curt was in in the nineties that ended over money.

We have never asked anybody for a deposit and nobody has ever not paid us.

items: PA: a powered mixer, two tops on poles, four vocal microphones, and a small sub that we take to the bars and leave home for the halls.
Our own backline, our own cables, our own stands, and a box of spares including the 9 volt batteries nobody else remembers.
Two 50 foot extension cords and one 100 foot, all 12 gauge.
A rug for under the drums, because Curt's kit walks on a hall floor.
About twenty koozies, whether you want them or not. See [url=/merch]the merch page[/url].
Two 20 amp circuits that are actually two circuits. Not two outlets on the same breaker, which is the commonest thing in the world and has cost us three quarters of an hour more than once.
A space about 14 feet by 10. We have fitted in less. We would rather not.
Somewhere to park a van and a pickup near the door for twenty minutes at each end.
Somewhere for the four of us to put our coats that is not the stage.
Water. That is it for food and drink as far as we are concerned. If you feed us we will eat it and be grateful and it is not in the price.

blocks.body:
[b]Weddings.[/b] We did one, in June 2025, for people we know, at the Eagles in Marchfield. It went fine. It also took four evenings of learning songs nobody in this band will ever play again, and there was a list of twenty-two requests, and a woman came up at half nine and asked us to learn something on the spot off her telephone.

We will do it for $500 and only for somebody one of us knows, and the honest answer is that you want a DJ and you will have a better night with one.

[b]Anything before 7pm that is not outdoors.[/b] We all work.

[b]Four sets.[/b] Three is what we have. If you want four hours we will do three sets and a longer break and play the last one long, and that is the same songs stretched out, and we will tell you that up front rather than pad it and hope you do not notice.

[b]Learning your song.[/b] Ask us four weeks out and Mike will very likely say yes, and he will learn it properly, and it will be right. Ask us on the night and the answer is no, and it is no because we are not good enough to do it badly and not mind.

[b]Are you insured?[/b] Yes. $1,000,000 general liability through the agency on Third Street in Gridfall, $310 a year, and the certificate names you if your hall needs it named. Three halls in this county need it and one of them is the Grange.

[b]How loud is it really?[/b] In a fire hall with the sub left at home we sit around where two people at a table can talk if they lean in. In a bar it is a bar. Come and ask at the break and we will bring it down for the next set and we will not resent it.

[b]Can you do quiet?[/b] For about an hour, yes, and we do it at the Legion on Veterans Day every year. Randy sits on the edge of the stage with the volume at two and it is a completely different band and some people prefer it.

[b]What happens if Mike gets called out?[/b] The three of us play instrumentals until he is back, or we finish the night without a singer, or if it is early we pack up and you pay us half, and that last one has never happened. In ten years he has gone out four or five times and twice he did not come back. It is the deal, and the deal is that about 900 households have water.
Places in this county that are worth your time, and a couple that are just here because they have been here since 2019.

blocks.label: People and places we actually use:

items.label: This site is best viewed with your eyes

blocks.body:
Two of those buttons do not go anywhere any more and I have left them up. The Wheelhouse one goes nowhere because the Wheelhouse is a storage unit business. The band exchange was a page a fellow in Halsey ran where you could find a drummer, and it went in about 2020, and it is the reason Randy is in this band.

The webring button is on here because I liked it and copied the code in 2019. We are not in the ring. I did read the rules and we do not fit any of the categories.

Almost all of it is second hand and almost all of it came from inside this county.

The powered mixer was $240 on [url=synth://gridfall-buysell.net/]Buy & Sell[/url] from a church in New Carrow that went to an all-in-one system. The tops were $180 for the pair off a fellow in Marchfield whose son had stopped DJ-ing. My cabinet was $110 with a blown driver.

[url=synth://gridfallswap.net/]GridfallSwap[/url] is where the wanted ads go now and it is where I found the 100 foot cord and where Curt got his cymbal bag. If you have a cable snake, a monitor wedge or a 1x15 cabinet sitting in a garage doing nothing, put it on there, and if it is any good I will very likely be the one who buys it.

I still read [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]the old boards[/url]. I cannot post, because they closed sign-ups years ago, and I have never asked anybody to let me in because I do not have anything to say that is worth somebody's trouble.

I turned signing off in March. It had been about twenty real messages in six years and then two or three a day of whatever this is, and I am leaving them up because deleting them one at a time was forty minutes I am not spending again.

The dates are all one day out since the host move. The real ones are near the bottom.

entries.body: Curt says you did Second Shift at the Grange and that the recording did not come out. Of course it did not. Play it anyway. I am fine, the girls are fine, and it is 71 degrees here in October which I cannot get used to.

entries.author: a man from Milbrook
entries.body: No hard feelings about Halsey. It was a nice drive and the diner at the crossroads was open. If you ever play Milbrook I will come to that too, although I understand nobody plays Milbrook.

entries.body: Bought a shirt at the fire hall Saturday. My husband says the tower looks like the tower, which from him is a rave. Do you do a large?

entries.author: Dean, Tilby's
entries.body: Put the October date on here Brian, people keep asking me and I am not your secretary.

blocks.body:
Made by hand in a text editor in 2019, off a template, and changed about once a season since. $18 a year for the name and $38 a year for the hosting.

There is no photos page. I started one twice. The photographs are on four different phones and one of them is Randy's and Randy's phone is in a drawer in a shop full of mowers.

If something here is out of date, it is out of date because nobody paid anybody to keep it, which is also true of most of the things worth reading about this county. The dates on [url=/shows]the shows page[/url] are right, though. Those I do keep.
